title: I used AI throughout development of my Unity arcade roguelite. The demo is finally playable
author: PerspectivePersonal
selftext:
I've been making FrogPop, a small arcade roguelite inspired by an old Flash game I used to play.

I used Claude and Codex for coding and debugging in Unity, and ChatGPT for some of the visual assets. I edited and integrated the generated art into the game.

AI could help get a feature working, but it could not tell me if it was fun. I still spent most of my time testing, tuning waves and bosses, and fixing things that broke elsewhere.

The free demo has the first 10 waves and runs in the browser or on Windows:

[https://blion247.itch.io/frogpop-demo](https://blion247.itch.io/frogpop-demo)

Has anyone else found that AI gets harder to use as a Unity project gets bigger?
